PullRequest.Title: sessions: stop the customization migration badge flickering
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to #343349; restores the behavior fixed in #338943 for #338621.

## Problem

The Customizations navigation icon repeatedly switches between the yellow migration indicator and the normal icon in Insiders 1.144.0 (`bdce63db5876`, macOS). The supplied screen recording shows this happening while the sidebar is idle.

#343349 reintroduced an unconditional reset of migration availability before asynchronous discovery. Every refresh therefore removes the badge, then restores it when the same migration hint is returned.

## Changes

- Preserve the last known migration availability until the current check completes.
- Retain ignored-group filtering, storage-change refreshes, cancellation guards, and clearing after a completed check returns no hint.
- Strengthen the existing regression test to assert that availability stays true during refreshes returning either the same hint or no hint, then updates to the completed result. Keep coverage for ignored/restored groups and disabled navigation.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --grep 'tracks the active customization total'` - failed before the product fix, with `refreshingState` and `removingState` false instead of true.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/chatCustomizationMigrationNotice.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatMigrationNotice.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 54 tests.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/customizationsNavigationState.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/customizationsToolbar.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- Commit hygiene hook - passed.
- Independent code review - approved, no actionable findings.

Fixed live Agents Window replay was not run; the maintainer approved proceeding with this limitation disclosed. No timers, listeners, discovery work, settings, persistence formats, or UI styling are added.

## Manual verification

1. Open the Agents Window with customization migrations available; confirm the yellow Customizations indicator is visible.
2. Trigger customization discovery updates repeatedly; confirm the indicator stays steady while checks are pending.
3. Ignore all remaining migration groups; confirm the indicator clears when discovery completes.
4. Restore a migration group; confirm the indicator returns.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each customization refresh forced a synchronous true-to-false observable notification and navigation-icon DOM rewrite before async migration discovery, followed by a second false-to-true rewrite when the same hint returned.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: The migration indicator repeatedly flickered in an otherwise idle Sessions sidebar, with redundant DOM icon updates on each customization refresh.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Deleting the eager false assignment preserves the last completed value while discovery is pending. An unchanged true result no longer produces an observable transition or icon DOM rewrite; a genuinely changed result still updates once after discovery completes.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base-revision line synchronously set migrationAvailable from true to false before every async computeMigrationHint refresh. That observable feeds SessionSectionRenderer.customizationsIcon; renderSessionHeaderIcon's autorun responds by clearing the icon node and rewriting its class, color, and display, then repeats those DOM writes when the unchanged hint resolves true. onDidChangeCustomizations can fire while the Sessions navigation is visible, so each refresh caused the reported visible indicator flicker and two unnecessary render transitions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions navigation is visible with migrations available, then customization/configuration/storage/harness changes trigger migration-hint refreshes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The CustomizationsNavigationState autorun synchronously reads ignored-group storage and starts computeMigrationHint; the final availability result waits for all five migration branches. The existing navigation badge remains usable and visible while discovery is pending, so discovery is not on the path to interacting with the sidebar, only on the path to committing a changed badge result. The diff removes the pre-discovery false notification and its synchronous icon DOM rewrite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files for agent, instructions, prompt, and skill types across user/workspace storage and extension providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six logical listPromptFiles calls arise from the three file-migration branches, but duplicate agent and instructions requests coalesce onto per-type cached promises; effective cold cardinality is at most four distinct type scans, and warm cardinality is zero scans until invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same computeMigrationHint call and the same cold/warm scan cardinality occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold scans must complete before the new migration hint can be committed; warm cached promises avoid the filesystem/provider scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve destination source folders for candidate target types; the active agent-host implementation waits for customization readiness and then reads in-memory host customization state, while extension-backed implementations may cross the extension-host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider call per distinct target type within each of the three file-migration branches, not per candidate; zero when no candidates exist. Agent-host readiness is cached per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider calls, grouping, readiness cache, and cancellation existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These grouped calls complete before each file-migration branch and therefore before the hint result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute the MCP migration plan from one acquired support scope, including configuration/file/secret-backed planning where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one MCP migration computation per hint refresh, grouped across all MCP servers rather than one boundary call per server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single grouped MCP branch ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs as one of five parallel branches and must settle before the final hint is committed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List configured plugin marketplaces from the agent host when user marketplace candidates exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero calls when no configured candidates exist; otherwise one agent-host request per hint refresh, independent of marketplace count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same conditional single request per refresh existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with the other migration branches and must settle before hint completion when invoked.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The CPU/filtering work scales linearly with discovered customization and migration-candidate counts. Expensive discovery is grouped by prompt/target type or whole MCP/marketplace inventory, with duplicate prompt-type requests coalesced rather than scaling per customization.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: computeMigrationHint launches five migration branches with Promise.all. Distinct prompt-type scans may run concurrently; source-folder calls are sequential within each branch, while branches remain parallel. A rerun disposes the prior autorun store and cancels its token, preventing stale completion from committing; the diff leaves scheduling and cancellation unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt file locations use per-type promise caches that coalesce concurrent duplicate requests and are invalidated by file/provider events; failed or cancelled computations clear their cache entry. Agent-host source-folder readiness is cached per session. computeMigrationHint itself is not cached and is rerun for each relevant signal, but the diff does not change those signals or calls. The observable suppresses unchanged completed values, and removing the eager false transition avoids defeating that suppression.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line is only the deleted observable reset before the unchanged async call; traced callers, caches, cancellation, providers, and DOM consumer show no added expensive work and one removed intermediate render transition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact scan and provider latency depends on cache warmth, extension providers, workspace size, MCP configuration, and whether plugin marketplaces are configured. Those factors do not affect the conclusion because boundary count and concurrency are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change reduces synchronous UI work by avoiding a transient false badge render and does not alter discovery frequency, boundary fan-out, caching, concurrency, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customizations navigation is hidden/disabled, the active session disappears, or the presentation switches away from the treatment.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The autorun immediately sets availability false and returns when disabled or when there is no active session; no migration discovery boundary is crossed. Switching into the treatment enables one normal discovery refresh; switching out cancels the active autorun work through its reader store.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per visibility/session transition; no collection-scaled discovery occurs while disabled or sessionless.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No discovery runs while disabled/sessionless. Any prior refresh is cancelled on autorun replacement; enabling starts the unchanged Promise.all refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted on the disabled/sessionless early-return path. Enabling reuses the same downstream caches described for visible refreshes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both early-return branches remain present and unchanged, and cancelOnDispose still owns in-flight refresh cancellation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed behavior; the retained value is still explicitly cleared on disable and missing-session transitions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The deletion does not retain the badge across disable/session loss and does not keep expensive work alive.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced the production change from refresh triggers through migration discovery, caches, cancellation, provider boundaries, and navigation-icon rendering. No performance finding was introduced; the PR instead removes a redundant synchronous badge render, and that concrete regression fix was recorded against its introducing commit.
